ideas.pitch: An AI-powered web platform specifically tuned to assist students in parsing, visualizing, and systematically breaking down non-routine mathematics problems using symbolic math engines and graph-based reasoning.
ideas.title: NonRoutine Solver Copilot
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly aligns with the core thesis of Math-O-Stellar, which focuses on non-routine mathematics, pattern recognition, and flexible logical reasoning rather than standard curriculum memory.

ideas.pitch: A browser-based collaborative canvas for sketching out proofs and counterexamples for complex non-routine math contest questions with real-time algebraic verification.
ideas.title: AxiomProof Interactive
ideas.why_it_could_win: Targeting the specific format of the competition (browser-based platform and non-routine problem solving) makes this immediately appealing to the event organizers and judges.

ideas.pitch: A machine learning pipeline that takes initial numerical sequences or geometric parameters from combinatorial problems and predicts general closed-form formulas and invariants.
ideas.title: MathPattern ML Forecaster
ideas.why_it_could_win: Draws heavily on the winning Poisson regression forecasting pattern by applying statistical modeling and pattern recognition directly to mathematical sequence problems.

ideas.pitch: A graph intelligence tool that maps logical dependencies in multi-step mathematical proofs to spot circular reasoning and missing premises in non-routine problem solutions.
ideas.title: ProofGraph Analytics
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages complex graph intelligence architectures seen in successful security and AML hackathon wins, adapting them to the domain of mathematical logic and rigorous verification.

ideas.pitch: An automated grading and formatting checker tailored for non-routine math competition answer files, ensuring algebraic expressions and logical steps are parseable before final submission.
ideas.title: MathOStellar Submission Verifier
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves a pain point familiar to both participants and organizers handling uploaded answer files and browser-based platform constraints during time-sensitive contests.
